title: The Remains of the Prophet
next_chapter_hook: The words in the Jade Slip, 'The Chen bloodline, generation after generation, all are chess pieces'—exploded like thunder in his mind. Had Chen Ji, all his struggles and schemes over the years, never escaped the chessboard?

text.content:
Ling Yuan.

The name pierced Chen Ji's heart like an ice pick, freezing his blood. The fading figure had said nothing, yet left this name at the last moment.

'Ling Yuan... Old Sect Master...' Chen Ji repeated in a low voice, his knuckles whitening. He remembered clearly—three years ago at the Sect Competition, it was Ling Yuan who personally awarded him, patting his shoulder and saying, 'Though his talent is ordinary, his composure is steadfast; his future is boundless.' He had thought it was merely an elder's perfunctory praise. Now, reconsidering, the depths hidden within those clouded old eyes far exceeded his imagination.

夜清 beside him sensed his unusual state, her brow furrowing slightly: 'What's wrong?'

Chen Ji drew a deep breath, suppressing the chill within. His voice regained its usual calm: 'Nothing. Let's go—the truth lies ahead.'

dialogue.content: 夜清 didn't immediately follow, but glanced at him sideways. How keen was a Holy Sect Demoness's perception—she had seen clearly Chen Ji's momentary loss of composure, yet she made no inquiries, merely remarking coolly: 'You said Ling Yuan was the former Sect Master of Tianqing Sect. I've researched this person—he suddenly entered seclusion twenty years ago and rarely appeared afterward. Why would a dying man want to see you?'

text.content:
Chen Ji's footsteps halted.

A dying man.

He recalled that figure's aged face, the feeble aura like a candle flame in the wind as it faded away. Something in his heart suddenly tensed. Was Ling Yuan about to die? Or rather... had Ling Yuan already been dead for some time?

'His meeting me wasn't for old times' sake.' Chen Ji continued forward, his voice carrying a coldness even he hadn't noticed. 'Whether alive or dead, I've，记住了 this name. When matters here are concluded, I'll personally go ask this old Sect Master—what exactly has he been scheming against me.'

Ahead, a massive gate of green jade stood at the corridor's end. Its surface covered in dense inscriptions, faintly radiating an aura similar to the Tianji Record.

dialogue.content:
'This gate...' Chen Ji reached out to touch the door, a tingling vibration flowing through his fingertips. 'It shares the same source as the Tianji Record.'

夜清 approached, her slender fingers hovering above the inscriptions, her expression unusually grave: 'These characters... I've seen them before. The forbidden texts of the Holy Sect mentioned that in ancient times, there existed beings called 'Heavenly Secrets Messengers' who could peer into destiny. The Tianji Record was their most precious legacy.' She paused. 'It's said that every Heavenly Secrets Messenger's final destination is to return here.'

Chen Ji said nothing. His gaze穿透 the gate, as though he had already glimpsed the scene beyond it.

The Heavenly Secrets Messenger's final destination... that was where the Prophet's remains lay.

text.content:
The green jade gate silently opened under Chen Ji's pushing palm.

The space beyond was unexpectedly vast and tranquil. This was an almost perfectly circular chamber, its vaulted ceiling carved with star maps, each celestial body faintly glowing, simulating some ancient, unchanging orbital pattern. At the chamber's center stood a white jade altar.

And upon the altar—

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply.

There sat a cross-legged corpse. Its preservation was startling—the skin, though dried, clung tightly to the bones; the facial features remained faintly discernible: a man approximately forty years old, with emaciated, refined features, the corners of his lips seemingly retaining a hint of an enigmatic smile, as though merely fallen into slumber.

The corpse's hands were cupped before its knees, cradling a jade slip that emitted a haunting glow.

dialogue.content:
夜清 drew a sharp breath: 'This... how is this possible? At such a level of preservation, it must be at least ten thousand years old.' She stepped closer, staring at the corpse's features. 'And this face... I've seen it in Holy Sect portraits.'

Chen Ji had already walked to the altar. His heart raced, his blood seemingly boiling—not from fear, but from some inexplicable resonance. He stared at that refined, emaciated face, and a familiar sensation washed over him.

Those eyebrows, that contours...

'He and I... share some resemblance.' Chen Ji murmured, his voice carrying rare uncertainty.

choice.prompt: The jade slip in the corpse's hands emanated an enticing glow; within it surely lay the truth of the shackles. Yet Chen Ji felt an inexplicable unease rising in his heart—did this corpse's similar features to his own imply some bloodline connection?

choices.text: Immediately remove the jade slip and examine it
choices.description: The truth lies right before my eyes; any risk is worth taking. The secret of the shackles concerns whether I can escape the Tianji Record's backlash.
choices.visible_reward: Complete information about the truth of the shackles
choices.risk_hint: The jade slip may be设有restriction

text.content:
Chen Ji didn't hesitate long. He reached out, and the moment his fingertips touched the jade slip, a wave of warmth surged into his body through his arm. It was an odd yet familiar sensation, as though some connection had been established at this moment.

The jade slip came loose in his hand, without the expected counter-blow from any barrier.

choices.text: First pay respects, then take the jade slip
choices.description: Since this may be an ancestor's remains, proper etiquette cannot be neglected. Moreover, given his cautious nature, showing reverence before touching unknown objects might prevent triggering certain barriers.

text.content:
Chen Ji drew a deep breath, stepped back, and clasped his hands together, bowing respectfully.

'Senior, regardless of who you are, regardless of what connection lies between us, your descendant today intrudes only to seek truth. If there is any offense, I humbly ask for your forgiveness.'

The moment his words fell, that faint smile on the corpse's lips seemed to deepen slightly. Then, the jade slip rose on its own, floating slowly toward Chen Ji.

The instant the jade slip entered Chen Ji's hand, the Heavenly Secrets Record on his chest suddenly trembled violently.

That一直沉寂的残页 actually began剧烈跳动 at this moment, as though sensing something. Chen Ji下意识地按住胸口, yet felt the rhythm of that beating gradually synchronize with his own heartbeat, then gradually diverge—as though some ancient existence was awakening.

Meanwhile, a faint glow appeared at the corpse's Brow Center. A wisp of residual consciousness, like gossamer threads, drifted out and coalesced before Chen Ji into a blurry phantom.

'Chen bloodline descendant... you have finally come.'

That voice was aged and weary, yet carried an indescribable relief.

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply: 'You... are still alive?'

The phantom slowly shook its head: 'This physical form died thirty thousand years ago. My consciousness was sealed here, merely to await the emergence of a Chen bloodline descendant powerful enough.'

'Thirty thousand years...' 夜清 beside him gasped—this number far exceeded her comprehension.

The phantom's gaze fell upon Chen Ji, as though trying to see through him: 'Your Tianji Record is incomplete, the shackles are deep, and destiny's backlash approaches... Time grows short, child.'

text.content:
Chen Ji forced himself to remain calm. He knew that although this wisp of残魂 was feeble, it held the information he desperately needed.

'Tell me, what is the truth of the shackles?' His voice was steady, only the knuckles gripping the jade slip faintly whitening. 'Why was the Tianji Record drawn to my Chen clan? How can I break this damned destiny?'

The phantom沉默了一瞬, a flicker of compassion seemingly appearing on its blurry features.

'You wish to know the truth?' Its voice suddenly grew very soft: 'Then first, you must understand one thing—'

'The Chen bloodline, generation after generation, all are chess pieces.'

This sentence struck Chen Ji's heart like a heavy hammer.

He felt his breath似乎停滞了一瞬. Those images flashed through his mind like a parade: his master saying 'You are the chosen one' before dying when he was seven; the destined般契合感 when the Tianji Record awakened at twelve; and that suffocating helplessness every time he peered into the future over these years...

So from the very beginning, he had never truly controlled his own fate.

'Hah...' Chen Ji suddenly低低laughed, that laughter carrying an indefinable bitterness and self-mockery. 'Chess pieces... what fine chess pieces.'

choice.prompt: The information revealed by the phantom shattered Chen Ji's understanding of fate. How should he face this cruel truth? Should he pursue it to the end, or first steady his mind?

choices.text: Inquire about the truth of the chess game
choices.description: Since he is a chess piece, he might as well ask clearly about the scale of the board. Who is playing this game? Where is the end of this chess game? Chen Ji has never feared the truth, no matter how cruel it is, he wants to know.

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes and took a deep breath. When he opened them again, the turmoil in his gaze had been replaced by cold rationality. 'Chess piece or discarded piece—I, Chen Ji, have never believed in destiny.' He spoke each word distinctly, 'Tell me, who is playing this game? Where are the boundaries of the board? Where is the endpoint?'

choices.text: Request to first examine the Jade Slip
choices.description: Words may be true or false, but a Jade Slip is a tangible object. Rather than listening to the remnant soul's account, he'd rather see the recorded contents with his own eyes.
choices.visible_cost: May miss the remnant soul's explanation
choices.risk_hint: The remnant soul may be dissatisfied

text.content: 'Wait.' Chen Ji raised his hand, interrupting the remnant soul. 'Rather than listening to you, I'd rather trust what I see myself.' He pressed the Jade Slip against his brow center, and his spiritual sense plunged into it. In an instant, information as vast as the sea flooded into his mind—like a tide, it brought revelations about the principles of the shackles, methods to break them, and... the true origin of the Chen bloodline.

The information in the Jade Slip was so vast that Chen Ji took quite a while to sort it out. It turned out that the so-called 'shackles' were not simply a curse or seal, but an extremely sophisticated contract—ancient times required a 'witness' to walk among humanity, selecting a group of humans with special bloodlines and implanting the Tianji Record Fragments into their bodies. These fragments would pass down through bloodlines for generations, and each inheritor would be gradually 'reclaimed' after awakening—the Tianji Record would drain their Heavenly Fate Value completely, ultimately leaving not even their souls behind. And the only way to break the shackles was to collect all nine pages of the Tianji Record, break free from Heaven's control, and become a truly independent 'chess player'.

dialogue.content: 'Nine pages...' Chen Ji murmured, his voice slightly hoarse. 'I only have three pages now. I need to find six more...' The phantom's voice sounded again: 'The nine pages of the Tianji Record are scattered everywhere, some are being secretly collected, and others are trying to destroy them. Ling Yuan... he was once a candidate for the Tianji Record, but was skipped over. What he hates isn't you, it's the Tianji Record itself.' Chen Ji abruptly raised his head: 'Are you saying—Ling Yuan wants to destroy the Tianji Record?' The phantom's form had become nearly invisible: 'Destroy... or monopolize. Either way, you will become his obstacle. So...'

text.content: Before the words finished, an intense pain suddenly erupted from the Tianji Record in Chen Ji's chest. The pain came without warning, as if something was being torn apart from within. He let out a muffled grunt, falling to one knee, cold sweat instantly beading on his forehead. Immediately after, he sensed a burning sensation where the fourth page should be—that was a reaction the fragment had never experienced before. 'This is...' Chen Ji fiercely tore open his robe, only to see the Tianji Record mark on his chest flickering intensely, the outline of the fourth page faintly visible, as if being forcibly pulled out by some power. Ye Qing cried out in alarm: 'Your Tianji Record... is unsealing?!'

dialogue.content: Chen Ji endured the excruciating pain, projecting his spiritual sense into the Tianji Record. He saw it—the fourth page was gradually emerging. On the yellowed paper's surface, dense text writhed like living creatures, ultimately condensing into content he had never seen before: 'The Heavenly Fate Lock Key is the other side of the Shackles' Eye. Two sides of one entity, generating and restraining each other. If you obtain one, you may peer into Heavenly Secrets; if the two merge as one...' The following content was blurred, as if deliberately erased by some power. But Chen Ji had already seen information shocking enough to shake his very being— The Heavenly Fate Lock Key. That was Chen Nian. His sister, missing for many years, was precisely one of the keys to breaking the shackles.

choice.prompt: The unsealing of the fourth page revealed a shocking truth—Chen Nian was not only his weakness but also the key to breaking the shackles. How should Chen Ji process this information?

choices.text: Immediately inquire about Chen Nian's whereabouts
choices.description: Since he knows his sister's importance, he can no longer wait. He needs to know where the Holy Sect took Chen Nian.
choices.visible_reward: Obtain clues about Chen Nian's location

text.content: Chen Ji abruptly raised his head, his burning gaze fixed on Ye Qing: 'Where is Chen Nian?' Ye Qing paused: 'Your sister?' 'Stop pretending.' Chen Ji's voice was ice-cold. 'You are the Holy Sect Saint of the Demonic Path. Do you expect me to believe you don't know that the Holy Sect took Chen Nian?' Ye Qing fell silent for a moment, then sighed: '...She is at the Holy Mountain. The Holy Sect guards her as their most precious sacrificial offering. If you want to take her away, you'd have to raze the entire Holy Sect.'

choices.text: First digest the information before acting
choices.description: The more critical the moment, the calmer one must stay. Revealing too much emotion now will only cause the situation to spiral out of control. First stabilize, then plan carefully.

text.content:
Chen Ji took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the surging emotions within.

Chen Nian... He had searched for her for so many years, only to discover that the answer had always been right in front of him. She was not a victim taken by the Holy Sect, but another piece on the board of fate, corresponding to him.

Was this truly the will of heaven, or the arrangement of some higher existence?

He closed his eyes, repeatedly contemplating this information in his heart. After a moment, he opened his eyes again, their depths restored to their usual depth and composure.

"I understand." he said, his voice terrifyingly calm. "This matter... will be considered carefully."

The phantom's voice rang out once more, this time so faint it was nearly inaudible: "Child... remember... though the chessboard is vast... a piece can also... become a player..."

As the words faded, the residual consciousness completely returned to nothingness. The remains began turning to ashes at this moment, as if completing some mission, finally able to rest in peace.

Only the Jade Slip remained quietly in Chen Ji's palm, its ethereal glow considerably dimmed, yet the information within remained clearly legible.

Chen Ji rose to his feet, placing the Jade Slip into his storage bag. His expression betrayed little turmoil, only an inexplicable flame burning in the depths of his eyes.

Ling Yuan. Chen Nian. Heavenly Eye.

These people, these matters, were gradually weaving into a vast web he had never glimpsed before. And he would personally overturn this chess game.

dialogue.content:
Ye Qing stepped forward, unusually refraining from any sarcastic or teasing remarks. She simply stood quietly at Chen Ji's side, her gaze falling upon his hand gripping the Jade Slip—that hand was trembling slightly.

"Are you alright?" she asked.

Chen Ji glanced at her, the corner of his lips curving slightly: "What, worried about me?"

"Don't flatter yourself." Ye Qing turned her face away. "I just don't want my partner to collapse before finding my mother."

Chen Ji laughed lightly, that laugh carrying an indefinable quality: "Rest assured, I Chen Ji never do anything without certainty. The information gained today is more than enough—Let's go. When we return, I need to sort through my thoughts carefully."

text.content:
The two retraced their path. Passing through layers of restrictions and exiting the ancient teleportation formation, when sunlight fell upon Chen Ji's face once more, he suddenly stopped.

"Ye Qing."

"Hmm?"

"If one day, I become an enemy of your Holy Sect..." Chen Ji didn't turn around, his voice soft. "What would you choose?"

Ye Qing fell silent for a moment, then laughed lightly: "You're quite frank."

"I just want to know the answer."

Ye Qing stepped forward, standing shoulder to shoulder with him, gazing at the distant horizon: "The Holy Sect never treated me as human. I have no sense of belonging to them whatsoever. But..." she paused, "I won't easily betray my clan."

Chen Ji nodded: "That's enough."

He said nothing more. Some answers need not be spoken—actions will prove everything.

Night wind brushed past, carrying a hint of early autumn's coolness.

Chen Ji suddenly thought of the name left behind by that dissipating figure—Ling Yuan. That old man he had once regarded as an elder, that seemingly gentle but deeply treacherous former Sect Master.

Thirty thousand years... This current Sect Master was only over three hundred years old, far from thirty thousand. But the remains clearly pointed to Tianqing Sect's former Sect Master when mentioning 'Ling Yuan.'

Could it be... that Ling Yuan is also connected to the Chen bloodline?

Or perhaps that dissipating figure wasn't referring to Ling Yuan himself, but to some existence related to him?

In any case, this name must be thoroughly investigated.

The words from the Jade Slip—'Chen bloodline, every generation is merely a piece'—exploded like thunder. Had his struggles and scheming all these years never escaped the chessboard?
